programme.title: Art of America
programme.desc: Andrew Graham-Dixon gets under the skin of the modern American metropolis. Beginning at the Statue of Liberty, he discovers how the ambitions of visionary artists and architects helped America remove itself from the shadow of Europe. In Manhattan, he explores the grimy world of early 20th century painters John Sloan and George Bellows, and visits Stockbridge in Massachusetts to explore Norman Rockwell's oeuvre.

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances

programme.title: A History of Britain by Simon Schama
programme.desc: A look at how the liberal politics and free-market economics of the British Empire in the 19th century unravelled, leading to the potato famine in Ireland and mutiny in India. By the early 20th century, nationalist movements around the globe had turned their back on the British 'workshop of the world'.

programme.title: Muhammad Ali
programme.desc: In the 'Fight of the Century' Muhammad Ali takes on his rival Joe Frazier. Ali loses, but becomes a hero nonetheless.

programme.title: Muhammad Ali
programme.desc: The Supreme Court overturns Muhammad Ali's conviction, validating his refusal to serve in the war in Vietnam. In 1974, Ali outduels Frazier, his greatest rival, in their highly anticipated rematch. But to complete his comeback, he must face the fearsome George Foreman.

programme.title: Muhammad Ali
programme.sub-title: Round Four: The Spell Remains, Part 1
programme.desc: Muhammad Ali shocks the world when he defeats George Foreman in the Rumble in the Jungle in Zaire, winning back the heavyweight title and becoming the most famous man on earth. He then faces Joe Frazier, his great rival, for a third time in the brutal Thrilla in Manila.

programme.title: Muhammad Ali
programme.sub-title: Round Four: The Spell Remains, Part 2
programme.desc: Muhammad Ali retired in 1981. In 1984, he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. Despite his illness, he continued to travel the world spreading his Islamic faith and became a symbol of peace and hope.

programme.title: Universe
programme.desc: Professor Brian Cox begins his exploration of the cosmos with a hymn to the great luminous bodies that bring light and warmth to the universe: the stars. It is estimated that there are two hundred trillion stars in the universe, each playing their part in an epic story of creation, a great saga that stretches from the dawn of time, with the arrival of the first star, through diverse generations until the arrival of our own star, the Sun, and a civilisation that has grown up in its light.

programme.title: Laurence Rees Remembers: The Nazis - A Warning from History
programme.desc: Laurence Rees' 1997 series explored the reasons why Germany fell in thrall to the Nazis. Combining archive, storytelling and interviews with figures at the heart of Hitler's rise to power, it tells us of the Nazi mentality and more.

programme.title: The Nazis: A Warning From History
programme.desc: Unearthing the shocking truth about how a cultured nation at the heart of Europe allowed a monster like Hitler to come to power. This film reveals how the Nazi party was born, and how, by January 1933, Germany voted for a Chancellor who was openly committed to overthrowing democracy.

programme.title: Ken Loach Remembers-The Old Oak
programme.desc: Ken Loach reflects on The Old Oak, his deeply moving portrait of solidarity, displacement and community in a former mining village in County Durham. Set against the arrival of Syrian refugees in a town scarred by austerity and deindustrialisation, the film explores whether compassion and collective action can survive in fractured times.

programme.title: The Old Oak
programme.desc: A pub landlord in a previously thriving mining community struggles to hold onto his pub. Meanwhile, tensions rise in the town when Syrian refugees are placed in the empty houses in the community.

programme.title: Ken Loach Remembers-Up the Junction
programme.desc: Ken Loach discusses Up the Junction, his landmark 1965 contribution to the BBC's The Wednesday Play strand, adapted from Nell Dunn's celebrated stories of working-class life in Battersea. Blending drama with documentary realism, the production shocked audiences with its frank depiction of sex, illegal abortion and everyday poverty, attracting record complaints while redefining television drama in Britain.

programme.title: The Wednesday Play
programme.desc: Classic play by Nell Dunn about three working-class young women who live, work and play in Battersea.

programme.title: The Wednesday Play

programme.title: This Cultural Life
programme.desc: Over six decades, Ken Loach has forged a reputation as Britain's foremost politically engaged film-maker, exploring issues of social justice, freedom and power. Ken talks to John Wilson about the key moments in his life that helped shaped his creativity. From his Midlands childhood as the son of a factory worker and annual summer holidays in Blackpool to his love for Czech cinema, which would become a huge inspiration on his own career.

programme.title: The Making of King Arthur
programme.desc: Simon Armitage traces the evolution of the Arthurian legend through the literature of the medieval age and reveals that King Arthur is not the great national hero he is seen as. He's a fickle and transitory character who was appropriated by the Normans to justify their conquest.

programme.title: Unforgiven
programme.desc: Uncompromising western about a reformed murderer who reluctantly agrees to one more killing. Long after he has settled into a peaceful life as a farmer with his two children, he is coaxed out of retirement by a young gun who wants his help in killing some men to collect a bounty.

programme.title: Arena
programme.sub-title: Clint Eastwood: Part One - Out of the West
programme.desc: Clint Eastwood recalls his tough childhood and looks back at his early career, from 'Rawhide' to 'Dirty Harry' and the spaghetti westerns. With contributions from Don Siegel, Sergio Leone, Eli Wallach and Martin Scorsese, plus an exclusive interview with his mother, Ruth.

programme.title: Arena
programme.sub-title: Clint Eastwood: Part Two - American Film-maker
programme.desc: Arena's profile of Clint Eastwood continues with his directorial debut, 'Play Misty for Me', which he completed in five weeks before going on to huge success in 'Dirty Harry'. Featuring actors Gene Hackman and Meryl Streep, director Martin Scorsese, plus Eastwood's mother Ruth and wife Dina.

programme.title: Howie Shorts

programme.title: Tomos a'i Ffrindiau
